case_sheet.raw_narrative: I enrolled my son Rohan in a 2-year JEE foundation coaching course at Apex Career Institute Kota on July 10, 2024. The institute demanded a full advance annual fee of ₹1,40,000 upfront, which I paid via Net Banking. During counseling, they promised a premium batch with a 1:35 teacher-student ratio and senior IITian faculty. However, when classes started on August 1, they merged 4 batches together into a massive auditorium with over 190 students, and the mathematics faculty was abruptly replaced by an inexperienced college graduate who read off PowerPoint slides. My son could neither ask doubts nor follow the lessons. On August 16 (after only 15 days of attendance), I submitted a formal written application requesting course discontinuation and pro-rata refund of the unutilized 11.5 months fees (approx ₹1,25,000). The center director rejected the application, pointing to a small clause at the bottom of the fee receipt: 'Fees once paid is non-negotiable and strictly non-refundable under any circumstances whatsoever.' I have the fee receipt, bank transaction statement, the written withdrawal application with stamped receipt acknowledgment, and photos of the overcrowded 190-student lecture hall.

rights_explainer.standing_summary: You have a strong legal standing under Indian civil and consumer law. Under Coaching & EdTech Advance Fee Disputes, withholding your legitimate funds of ₹140,000 or failing to deliver contracted quality is legally actionable. Indian law does not allow unilateral contract clauses or arbitrary forfeitures.
key_rights: **Consumer Protection Act, 2019 (Section 2(46))**: Standard clauses stating 'Fees once paid will not be refunded under any circumstances' are unconscionable and legally void under Section 2(46).
**CCPA Guidelines for Prevention of Unfair Trade Practices in Coaching Sector, 2024 (Guideline 4 & 5)**: Mandatory pro-rata refund of unutilized course fee within 10 days of exit request.
**Supreme Court & NCDRC Landmark Precedents (FIITJEE Ltd. vs. Minathi Nayak & Brilliant Tutorials precedents)**: Coaching institutes are service providers amenable to Consumer Forum jurisdiction.
authorities: District Consumer Disputes Redressal Commission (DCDRC) via e-Daakhil
rights_explainer.limitation_period: 2 years from the date of withdrawal/refund refusal.

escalation_path.tier: Step 1: Formal Statutory Demand Notice (15-Day Cure Period)
escalation_path.action: Dispatch a formal legal notice via Registered Post AD / Speed Post and Email. Give them 15 working days to refund ₹140,000 plus interest.
escalation_path.why_it_works: Over 75% of Indian consumer & tenancy disputes settle at this stage once the opposite party sees precise statutory sections and realizes you are prepared to escalate.

escalation_path.tier: Step 2: National Consumer Helpline (NCH 1915) / Statutory Portal
escalation_path.action: File a grievance on consumerhelpline.gov.in (Toll-Free 1915) or INGRAM portal.
escalation_path.why_it_works: Government officers directly notify the nodal officer of the registered corporate entity, requiring a mandatory written status update within 30 days.

escalation_path.tier: Step 3: Online e-Daakhil / District Consumer Commission (DCDRC)
escalation_path.action: File an e-complaint on e-daakhil.nic.in before the District Consumer Forum. Under the Consumer Protection Act 2019, claims up to ₹5 Lakh have ZERO court fees.
escalation_path.why_it_works: You do NOT need to hire an expensive advocate; consumers can represent themselves. The forum can award refund + 9-12% interest + compensation for mental harassment.
escalation_path.cost: ₹0 (for claims up to ₹5L), ₹200 for claims up to ₹10L

rights_explainer.realistic_timeline: 15 days for initial notice response; 30 to 45 days if escalated via NCH; 3 to 6 months for formal Consumer Commission order.
rights_explainer.financial_outlook: Eligible to claim full ₹140,000 + 9-12% annual interest + ₹15,000 to ₹25,000 for mental agony & litigation costs.

FORMAL LEGAL DEMAND NOTICE (WITHOUT PREJUDICE)
DISPATCHED VIA: REGISTERED POST WITH A.D. / SPEED POST & OFFICIAL EMAIL
================================================================================

DATE: 08 November, 2026

TO:
Coaching Institute / Management
[Full Registered Address / Corporate Office / Residential Address]
Email: [Official Email / Nodal Grievance Officer]

FROM:
[Complainant / Aggrieved Citizen Name]
[Residential Address / Contact Phone / Email]

SUBJECT:
DEMAND NOTICE FOR IMMEDIATE REFUND OF INR 140,000/- WITH ACCRUED INTEREST
AND COMPENSATION FOR DEFICIENCY IN SERVICE, WRONGFUL RETENTION, AND UNFAIR TRADE PRACTICE.

SIR / MADAM,

Under explicit instructions and on behalf of my client / self, the present Legal Notice is hereby served upon you:

1. FACTUAL BACKGROUND & TRANSACTION DETAILS:
   a) That the Claimant entered into a valid and lawful commercial/tenancy/service transaction with you, wherein full payment/deposit of INR 140,000/- was duly remitted.
   b) I enrolled my son Rohan in a 2-year JEE foundation coaching course at Apex Career Institute Kota on July 10, 2024
   c) That despite multiple written communications, emails, and follow-ups, you have wilfully failed, neglected, and refused to remediate the defect / return the legitimate funds due to the Claimant.

2. STATUTORY VIOLATIONS & LEGAL GROUNDS:
   Under the CCPA Guidelines for Prevention of Unfair Trade Practices in Coaching Sector (2024) and established NCDRC precedents (including FIITJEE Ltd. vs. Minathi Nayak), non-refundable advance fee clauses are legally void and unconscionable under Section 2(46) of the Consumer Protection Act, 2019. Retention of unearned course fees for services not availed constitutes an Unfair Trade Practice.

3. WRONGFUL RETENTION & DAMAGES:
   By virtue of your arbitrary conduct, the Claimant has suffered severe financial distress, inconvenience, and mental agony. You have illegally retained money that does not belong to you, depriving the Claimant of its rightful use.

4. REQUISITE DEMANDS & 15-DAY CURE NOTICE:
   You are hereby formally called upon to:
   i. Immediately refund the principal amount of INR 140,000/- (Indian Rupees 140,000 only) into the Claimant's designated bank account within 15 (FIFTEEN) DAYS of the receipt of this Notice;
   ii. Pay interest calculated at the rate of 12% per annum from the date the amount fell due until the date of actual payment;
   iii. Pay an amount of INR 15,000/- towards damages for mental harassment and costs incurred in issuing this formal notice.

TAKE NOTICE that if you fail to comply with the legitimate demands set forth above within the stipulated period of 15 days, the Claimant shall be constrained to institute appropriate legal proceedings against you, including filing a formal Consumer Complaint under Section 35 of the Consumer Protection Act, 2019 before the Competent District Consumer Disputes Redressal Commission / Civil Court of competent jurisdiction, entirely at your sole risk, cost, and consequences.

A copy of this Legal Notice is retained in records for future legal proceedings.

Yours faithfully,

_____________________________
[Complainant / Authorized Signatory]
Enclosures:
1. Proof of Payment / Bank Statement
2. Written Agreement / Booking Confirmation
3. Relevant WhatsApp / Email Communication Records

roleplay_scenarios.objection: You signed the admission form acknowledging that fees once paid is strictly non-refundable under any circumstances. We cannot make an exception.
roleplay_scenarios.intent: Citing one-sided boilerplate contract to withhold advance tuition.
roleplay_scenarios.rebuttal_english: The Supreme Court of India and NCDRC in landmark judgments including FIITJEE vs Minathi Nayak have explicitly held that educational institutions cannot hoard advance fees if a student withdraws mid-way. Under the CCPA Coaching Guidelines 2024 and Section 2(46) of the Consumer Protection Act 2019, a 'no refund' clause is void as an Unfair Contract. You are legally required to refund the pro-rata unutilized fee within 10 days.
roleplay_scenarios.rebuttal_hinglish: Supreme Court aur NCDRC ne saaf bola hai ki coaching institutes poori advance fees forfeit nahi kar sakte. CCPA Coaching Guidelines 2024 aur Section 2(46) CPA ke under 'Non-refundable' clause illegal maana gaya hai. Aapko bache huye duration ki pro-rata fees 10 din ke andar refund karni hogi.
